cards.note: New card (debate): Relatable desi childhood memory that no other card covers.

cards.Name: Which indoor game kept you busy during load shedding as a kid (chor sipahi, name-place-animal-thing, carrom)?
cards.note: New card (debate): Indoor games during load shedding are a new angle. Card 532 covers outdoor gali games.

cards.Name: Which disappearing Pakistani tradition do you wish we could bring back?
cards.note: New card (debate): Distinct enough from 242 (a word or saying), 636 (passing on a family tradition), 571 and 89 (family traditions).

cards.Name: Has a dua of yours ever been answered in a way you did not expect?
cards.note: New card (debate): A worship-related personal question, which the owner allows. It differs from 732 (which dua you make most often).

cards.Name: What do you remember most about your school van or rickshaw rides?
cards.note: New card (debate): Shared school-commute nostalgia that no other card covers. 540 and 713 ask about rickshaw drivers and truck art, not school rides.

cards.Name: What is a disappointment that later turned out to be a blessing in disguise?
cards.note: New card (debate): A distinct reflective card that is different from the regret, tawakkul and risk cards.

cards.Name: What is one thing about your deen you would like to learn more about this year?
cards.note: New card (debate): A respectful faith-growth question that makes no factual claims and is not a duplicate.

cards.Name: Which elder in your family tells the same story at every gathering, and how does it go?
cards.note: New card (debate): Affectionate family humour that the deck does not have yet.

cards.Name: Who in your family is the worst at keeping a surprise secret?
cards.note: New card (debate): A light family question that invites a story and is not a duplicate.

cards.Name: Which relative's house has the best food at a dawat, and what do you always hope they make?
cards.note: New card (debate): Dawat food culture. Different from the Nani/Dadi dish card and the late-arrival card.

cards.Name: If you could spend one day 100 years ago in any city that is now in Pakistan, which would you pick and why?
cards.note: New card (debate): Challenger's amended version. It is worded accurately because Pakistan did not exist in 1926.

cards.Name: What is the funniest thing you have seen happen at iftar or taraweeh in the masjid?
cards.note: New card (debate): Worship-related personal questions are allowed. The humour is about people, not worship, and it differs from the existing masjid and iftar memory cards.

cards.Name: What is the funniest thing a guest has done while staying over at your house?
cards.note: New card (debate): Overnight guests are not covered by the existing guest cards.

cards.Name: Which teacher's catchphrase or habit do you still remember? Do your best impression.
cards.note: New card (debate): A playful school memory that is different from the favourite, strictest and embarrassing teacher cards.

cards.Name: Do you remember your first roza (roza kushai)? How did you get through the afternoon?
cards.note: New card (debate): Accurate, warm Ramadan childhood prompt; no existing card asks about the first fast.

cards.Name: Have you or someone in your family been on Umrah or Hajj? Which moment from the journey stayed with you most?
cards.note: New card (debate): Respectful worship-related personal question the owner allows; no Hajj/Umrah card exists and the wording includes players who have not gone.

cards.Name: Which uncle in your family has the strongest political opinions, and what does he always say at the dinner table?
cards.note: New card (debate): Politics is allowed; affectionate family roast with no politics card in the deck.

cards.Name: What is the funniest thing that happened when the lights went out in the middle of a dawat or wedding?
cards.note: New card (debate): Story prompt distinct from the existing load-shedding tip, lift and indoor-game cards.

cards.Name: Which cousin was the troublemaker at every family gathering, and what was their best stunt?
cards.note: New card (debate): Existing cousin cards cover closeness, arguments and funny sayings; this is new.

cards.Name: If you had to cook one deg for 50 guests tomorrow, which dish would you make?
cards.note: New card (debate): Desi cooking hypothetical not covered by 'best thing you cooked' or 'cooking vs going out'.

cards.Name: Who in your family guards the WiFi password like a state secret, and how do you get it out of them?
cards.note: New card (debate): New household joke; the only Wi-Fi card is about network names.

cards.Name: Which Pakistani road journey would you happily do again tomorrow (the Karakoram Highway, the Makran Coastal Highway, the Motorway from Lahore to Islamabad)?
cards.note: New card (debate): Challenger's amendment of P9: route-only examples avoid overlap with the existing 'trip up north (Murree, Swat, Naran, Hunza)' card and use the correct name for the Makran Coastal Highway.

cards.Name: If your family WhatsApp group were renamed to tell the truth, what would it be called?
cards.note: New card (debate): Creative naming prompt distinct from the existing 'funniest WhatsApp message' card.
